precepts.text: I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there, and have chosen David to be over my people.
precepts.point: Unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there shall ye seek: out of all the tribes he chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and the temple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.” Moses said the Lord would choose a place “out of all your tribes to put his name there”, and here is the choice: out of all the tribes he chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and the temple, and he chose David to be over his people Israel.

That is the habitation Israel was to seek and come to: “even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come”. The place was not left for Israel to pick; the Lord chose it, and the place where he put his name is Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The scepter and lawgiver stay with Judah, the line David came from.
precepts.point: When Israel came out of Egypt the Most High did not fix His house in a city. He chose Jerusalem, the city of David, for the temple, and He chose David to be over His people Israel.
precepts.why:
“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come.” The sceptre and the lawgiver stay with Judah, and Judah is the line David came from.

That is why, after bringing Israel out of Egypt and choosing no city and no man, the Most High says, “I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.” The choosing of David, a man of Judah, to rule over his people is the sceptre of Judah that Jacob spoke of, and Jerusalem, the city of David, is where his house would be built.

precepts.text: Israel shall know the Most High is in their midst, their God and none else, and shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: No other nation has this. The Most High promised Israel that in a drought, if they repented and returned to Him, He would honor their prayers and send rain in due season.
precepts.why:
“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

No other nation has this. When the heaven is shut up and there is no rain because Israel sinned, if they pray toward this place, confess his name and turn from their sin, the Most High promised to hear, forgive, teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and “send rain upon thy land, which thou hast given unto thy people for an inheritance.”

When he answers that repentance and sends the rain in due season, Israel knows he is in their midst, their God and none else, and they are not ashamed.

precepts.text: The Canaanite woman was healed only when she owned herself a dog and submitted under Israel; that faith moved Him.
precepts.point: The Most High hears the stranger who submits and fears Him, so all nations know the name attached to this house. He does not honor a prayer prayed against Israel or for dominion over His people.
precepts.why:
Christ told the Canaanite woman, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” She did not fight it. She said, “Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.” She owned herself a dog and submitted under Israel, and that faith moved him: “O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.”

That is the stranger Solomon prayed for, “which is not of thy people Israel, but is come from a far country for thy great name’s sake.” The Most High hears the stranger who submits and fears him, “that all people of the earth may know thy name, and fear thee, as doth thy people Israel.”

He does not honor a prayer prayed against Israel or for dominion over his people. The stranger is heard in the place of the dog under the master’s table, not in the place of the children.

precepts.text: The same word to David: he shall not fail a man to sit on the throne if his children keep the way.
precepts.point: The promise means every king of Israel would come through David's lineage. The kingdom continues so long as the house keeps the covenant.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Solomon had already prayed it back to the Most High: “keep with thy servant David my father that which thou hast promised him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit upon the throne of Israel; yet so that thy children take heed to their way to walk in my law.”

Now the Most High answers with the same word: if Solomon will walk before him as David walked and observe his statutes and judgments, “Then will I stablish the throne of thy kingdom, according as I have covenanted with David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man to be ruler in Israel.”

The promise means every king of Israel would come through David’s lineage. But it carries a condition: the kingdom continues so long as the house keeps the covenant and his children walk in his law.

precepts.text: I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.
precepts.point: Be silent, O all flesh, before the Lord: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation.

note.label: Zechariah 2: The Measuring Line and the Apple of His Eye

precepts.why:
The Lord shall choose Jerusalem again. That Jerusalem is chosen is said over and over in the scriptures. “But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.”

He chose Jerusalem for his name, and David over his people Israel. Judah is his portion in the holy land, and Jerusalem is the city he chooses again.

moments.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: If they sin against thee, (for there is no man which sinneth not,) and thou deliver them over before their enemies, and they carry them away captives unto a land far off or near: far off means scattered throughout the nations; near means close to Jerusalem.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: Yet if they bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive. Definition read in class: bethink means to remember, to recall, to cause oneself to be reminded or to consider. That is why the law says remember the Sabbath day; remember your heritage. The Sabbath is vital to our growth and understanding of our true heritage.

And turn and pray unto thee in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have done amiss, and have dealt wickedly. In captivity we must learn how to suffer and be delivered with righteousness: continue to keep God's commandments while under oppression. You say, I am not oppressed, I have no chains; but that spirit of clocking in and working tries to dim the flame you have. That is why you have to build your faith up and understand this is not our rest.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: Now I want to get into some examples of sovereignty, of when we once had sovereignty, when we were once a sovereign kingdom. The Lord establishes the leader, and the Lord establishes the sovereignty of a kingdom. A leader and his people. The Lord establishes all of that. It is not willy-nilly. You write some slick stuff down on a piece of paper and that makes you sovereign, that makes you ruler, that makes you not subject to the powers that be? That makes no sense at all. That is why on those videos you always see that so-called sovereign person, male or female, always get the wrong end of the baton. Every single time.

But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel. So David was sovereign. Israel at this time was sovereign. Why? Because the Lord established it. And the Lord established first and foremost a place, a country, a country for his people, and the king that he would have to reign over his people. That is what sovereignty looks like.

It does not look like one negro trying to evade taxes and trying to evade the laws of the land, a ticket, talking about he is sovereign, he is over something. All these little funny catchphrases they be having. That is not what the Lord has established. Neither is there any power in it. That is foolishness.
Solomon declared that the Most High had said He would dwell in the thick darkness, and that Solomon had built Him a house of habitation, a place for His dwelling for ever.
Solomon turned and blessed the whole congregation of Israel as they stood. The king led the nation in blessing before he led them in prayer.

Solomon blessed the Most High, who fulfilled with His hand what He spake with His mouth to David, that since bringing Israel out of Egypt He chose no city to build a house for His name, nor any man to rule, until He chose Jerusalem and David.
When Israel came out of Egypt the Most High did not fix His house in a city. He chose Jerusalem, the city of David, for the temple, and He chose David to be over His people Israel.
A right desire toward the Most High is counted good even when the task is given to another. David's heart was accepted though the building was assigned to Solomon.

It was in David's heart to build the house, and the Most High said he did well that it was in his heart, but David would not build it. His son who came forth of his loins would build the house for the name of the Most High.

The Most High performed His word, raising Solomon up in the room of David to sit on the throne of Israel, and Solomon built the house and put the ark there, in which is the covenant made with the children of Israel.
The promise ran from David to Solomon exactly as spoken. The ark and its covenant were set in the house that fulfilled the word.

Solomon stood before the altar in the presence of all the congregation and spread forth his hands, having made a brazen scaffold five cubits long, five broad, and three high, on which he kneeled before all Israel.
The king knelt in public before his people and spread his hands toward heaven, the same posture used in reading and prayer. Leadership bowed first.
Solomon prayed that there is no god like the Most High in heaven or earth, who keepeth covenant and sheweth mercy to servants that walk before Him with all their heart.
He acknowledged that the Most High had kept His promise to David and fulfilled it with His hand, as it was that day.
Solomon asked the Most High to keep the promise that David would not fail to have a man to sit on the throne of Israel, so long as his children take heed to walk in the law.
The throne stood on a condition. The line would continue if the children walked in the law as David walked. This is the same word later given to Solomon himself.
Solomon asked whether the Most High would in very deed dwell with man on earth, since heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him, how much less the house he had built.
Even with the house built, Solomon understood that the Most High could not be contained in it. He asked that the Most High have respect to the prayer of His servant.
Before we pray we ask the Most High to hear and honor the prayer, for He is not bound to hear when our own doings have shut His ear.
Solomon asked that the eyes of the Most High be open toward this house day and night, to hearken to the prayer His servant made toward the place where He said He would put His name.
He asked that the Most High hear from His dwelling place in heaven, and when He heard, forgive.

If a man sinned against his neighbor and an oath were laid on him to come before the altar in this house, Solomon asked the Most High to hear from heaven and judge, requiting the wicked and justifying the righteous.

If Israel were put to the worst before the enemy because they sinned, then turned, confessed His name, and prayed in this house, Solomon asked the Most High to forgive and bring them again to the land.
This pattern repeated through the history of Israel. The Most High raised saviors when the people prayed in captivity, forgave them, and returned them to the land.

If heaven were shut and there was no rain because of sin, and the people prayed toward this place, confessed His name, and turned from sin, Solomon asked the Most High to hear, forgive, and teach them the good way and send rain.
No other nation has this. The Most High promised Israel that in a drought, if they repented and returned to Him, He would honor their prayers and send rain in due season.

Whatever the plague, dearth, pestilence, blasting, mildew, locust, caterpiller, or siege, whatever prayer any man of Israel made knowing his own sore and grief, Solomon asked the Most High to hear and render to every man according to his ways.
The Most High alone knoweth the heart of the children of men. He answers according to what He sees in the heart, that the people may fear Him and walk in His ways in the land.

Concerning the stranger not of Israel who comes from a far country for His great name and prays toward this house, Solomon asked the Most High to hear, so that all people of the earth may know His name and fear Him as Israel does.
The Most High hears the stranger who submits and fears Him, so all nations know the name attached to this house. He does not honor a prayer prayed against Israel or for dominion over His people.
If Israel went to war against their enemies in the way He sent them and prayed toward the city and house, Solomon asked the Most High to hear their prayer and maintain their cause.
The Most High helps Israel in the way He sends them. An enemy praying to harm Israel does not get in the city, much less the temple; common sense reads the promise rightly.

Since there is no man that sinneth not, if Israel sinned and were carried captive far off or near, then bethought themselves and turned and prayed in the land of their captivity, confessing they had done wickedly, Solomon asked the Most High to hear and maintain their cause and forgive.

Read this as Solomon himself, standing before the whole nation, praying that even in captivity a repentant Israel would be heard. To maintain their cause is to uphold their right, the covenant that He would hear them when they turned back.

Solomon asked that the eyes and ears of the Most High be attentive to the prayer made in this place, that He arise to His resting place with the ark of His strength, that His priests be clothed with salvation and His saints rejoice in goodness.
He closed asking the Most High not to turn away the face of His anointed, but to remember the mercies of David His servant.
